question: Assume today is 2026-09-01. You know nothing published after this date. Estimate the total value of online shopping transactions in South Korea in August 2026, in Korean won (KRW), as it will be first reported in the national statistics agency's monthly Online Shopping Trends release (온라인쇼핑동향, National Data Office, formerly Statistics Korea).

target.what: Total value (in KRW) of online shopping transactions in South Korea during August 2026, as reported in the National Data Office (formerly Statistics Korea) monthly Online Shopping Trends (온라인쇼핑동향) release — i.e., the aggregate 'online shopping transaction value' (온라인쇼핑 거래액) covering online/mobile re
target.publisher: National Data Office (국가데이터처, formerly Statistics Korea) — Online Shopping Trends (온라인쇼핑동향)
target.caveats: Target period is completed relative to the 2026-09-01 cutoff but the August 2026 release would not yet be published (typically ~1 month lag, early October 2026), so no observed value exists at cutoff. Working interpretation: the headline total online shopping transaction value (거래액) in current KRW,

candidates.hypothesis: August 2026 total online shopping transaction value ≈ recent monthly level (e.g., mid-2026 months) adjusted for August seasonal factor and YoY growth trend. Own history gives level, seasonality (August vs July), and growth rate.
candidates.data_to_find: Monthly total online shopping transaction value (거래액) for 2023-2026 through the latest month published before 2026-09-01 (likely July 2026), plus August values for 2023, 2024, 2025 to derive August seasonal ratio and YoY growth. Minimum: last 12-24 monthly totals and the three prior August values.
search_hints: Statistics Korea online shopping trends monthly transaction value 2025 2026

candidates.hypothesis: Online shopping transaction value is a share of total retail sales (소매판매액) plus services; using the retail sales index or 소매판매액 total times the online penetration share gives an independent level estimate. Direction: online share has been rising, so apply a trended share.
candidates.data_to_find: Monthly total retail sales value (소매판매액지수 or 소매판매액) for 2025-2026 and the online shopping share of retail sales; also the online share of the covered service categories. Minimum: retail sales level for mid-2026 and online share.
search_hints: online shopping share of retail sales Korea 2025

candidates.hypothesis: Total = sum over commodity groups (food, household goods, apparel, electronics, cosmetics, services, travel, etc.) of group transaction values; summing latest group levels with August seasonality gives the total and reveals which groups drive August.
candidates.data_to_find: Latest monthly transaction value by commodity group (상품군별 거래액) for mid-2026 and prior Augusts; group-level YoY growth. Minimum: group breakdown for the most recent month and one prior August.
search_hints: online shopping transaction value by commodity group Korea

candidates.perspective: Mobile vs PC and domestic vs overseas split
candidates.hypothesis: Total = mobile + PC (or domestic + overseas); mobile share is high and stable, so a mobile transaction value estimate times 1/mobile-share gives the total. Overseas direct purchase/sale components add a small increment.
candidates.data_to_find: Monthly mobile (모바일) and PC online shopping transaction values for 2025-2026, and overseas direct purchase (해외직구) and overseas sales components. Minimum: mobile share for mid-2026 and the overseas component size.
search_hints: online shopping mobile PC transaction Korea

candidates.hypothesis: August 2026 has no major Korean gift-giving holiday, but summer vacation/travel, heat waves, and any major platform promotions or regulatory changes (e.g., e-commerce platform fee/payment rules, Coupang/Naver events) shift the level. Quantify deviation from trend.
candidates.data_to_find: Evidence of major August 2026 promotions, platform disruptions, weather/heat effects on online demand, and any policy changes affecting online transactions; compare with prior August anomalies. Minimum: documented events with measurable direction.

candidates.hypothesis: Published forecasts of Korea e-commerce/online retail market size for 2026 (annual) can be divided by 12 and adjusted for August share to cross-check the monthly total. Direction: forecasts give an annual anchor.
candidates.data_to_find: Annual 2026 Korea online shopping/e-commerce market size forecasts (KRW) from industry bodies, research firms, or government plans; monthly average implied. Minimum: one credible annual 2026 forecast with scope matching the survey.

candidates.hypothesis: Total transaction value ≈ number of online card/e-payment transactions × average transaction value; card/payment network aggregates (e.g., BC, Shinhan, Bank of Korea payment statistics) provide an independent flow measure that can be scaled to the survey coverage.
candidates.data_to_find: Monthly online/e-commerce card payment value or transaction counts for 2026 (Bank of Korea 지급결제동향, card company e-commerce stats) and average online transaction value. Minimum: online card payment value for a recent month and its relation to the survey total.

Historical August/July pairs (e.g., 2024, 2025) would quantify whether August runs above or below July, resolving the largest uncertainty in the YoY-scaling route.
directions.data_to_find: Total online shopping transaction value for July and August in 2023, 2024, 2025 (and ideally the monthly seasonal pattern).
search_hints: Statistics Korea online shopping August seasonal monthly table

directions.hypothesis: Any August 2026 partial data (e.g., card-network online spend, platform GMV, or a first-20-day figure) would anchor the level directly and resolve whether the July 2026 momentum (7.3% YoY) held, accelerated, or faded in August. This is the single most valuable missing input for the target month.
directions.data_to_find: August 2026 online card/e-payment spend or platform GMV aggregates, or any partial-month online retail indicator for August 2026.

methods.label: m1
methods.rationale: Repaired: the original signal (p46/p51) had no 2025 value, so yoy_scaling could not align years. Now the signal is the YoY growth rate itself, with a3 supplying the 2026 value (July 2026 +7.3% momentum, p51) and p51 supplying 2025's July growth for alignment; target history is August 2025 (p1). Shared dependency on the official series and on July momentum persisting into August.
notes: mixed % and non-% units; dropped the minority

methods.label: m2

p46.role: Total online shopping transaction value, South Korea, July 2026 (most recent observed month)

a2.role: August-to-July seasonal ratio of total online shopping value

methods.rationale: July 2026 level (p46) times an August/July seasonal ratio (a2) grounded in 2023–2025 Aug/Jul ratios. Captures level and seasonality; fails if August 2026 deviates from historical seasonal pattern.

methods.label: m3

p1.role: Total online shopping transaction value, South Korea, August 2025

a1.role: August 2026 YoY growth of total online shopping value

methods.rationale: August 2025 total (p1) grown by an assumed August 2026 YoY rate (a1) anchored on July 2026's +7.3% (p51). Direct year-over-year route; fails if August 2026 growth diverges sharply from July.

weight_basis.m2: B1 of 2 blocks; geometric mean of blocks
weight_basis.m3: B2 of 2 blocks; geometric mean of blocks

combination.weight_gate: off: inverse backtest-error weights need a bank-level gate (>= 30 scored questions with >= 2 backtested routes, hit rate >= 0.7; METHODS_ZH 4.1), which has not been run

m3.note: Monte Carlo width below the default, not used to narrow

interval.rule: several blocks: root mean square of the block widths, times the Birge ratio when it exceeds 1

baseline.rule: seasonal naive: the target's value for the same calendar period last year

kept.name: August 2026 YoY growth of total online shopping value
kept.rationale: July 2026 ran +7.3% (p51); 2025 monthly YoY ranged 0.6–13.3% with a mid-year dip then rebound. August has no gift holiday; summer travel/appliance demand supports a similar pace. Range spans a slowdown to ~4% and a re-acceleration to ~10%.
kept.applies_when: August 2026 momentum resembles July 2026 rather than a sharp break.
kept.falsified_by: Card-network or platform data showing August 2026 YoY well below 4% or above 10%.

kept.name: August-to-July seasonal ratio of total online shopping value
kept.rationale: Historical Aug/Jul ratios: 2023 203.591/201.296=1.011; 2024 210.875/214.622=0.983; 2025 22.4802/23.0335=0.976. Ratios cluster near 0.98–1.01; range allows for summer-vacation uplift or post-July cooling.
kept.falsified_by: Evidence of an unusual August 2026 promotion or heatwave shifting the ratio outside 0.93–1.07.

kept.name: August 2026 YoY growth of total online shopping value (yoy_scaling signal)
kept.rationale: Same basis as a1: July 2026 +7.3% (p51) is the latest observed momentum; August 2025 grew 6.6% (p3) and 2025 monthly growth ranged 0.6–13.3%. Used as the signal for the yoy_scaling route because no kept point gives August 2026 growth directly.
kept.applies_when: August 2026 growth is close to July 2026's pace.
kept.falsified_by: Any August 2026 partial data showing growth outside 4–10%.

published.note: not checked: backtest or scored question (as_of before today, or an official value is registered), so the target cannot have been published by as_of

by_construction: Only URLs leave the searcher (code regex); extractor, judge and final prompts never contain search result titles, snippets or the searcher's text. This holds by construction and is not measured.
residual_risks: The searcher sees post-cutoff search results and chooses which URLs are fetched, so page selection can be conditioned on the answer; only the URLs leave the searcher, and in backtests every fetched page is a snapshot dated <= as_of.
Live pages are used only when as_of is today; in backtests every page is an archived snapshot dated <= as_of.
The leak sentinel only catches registered official values in common formats, not paraphrased or derived numbers.
The model's own training data (knowledge cutoff unpublished) can include history before as_of; it cannot include the target if the target was published after the model's release.
Wayback snapshots are captured by a third party; a snapshot date <= as_of proves the content existed by then.
Assumption values are proposed by the judge model from its own knowledge, which can include the target's history before as_of; code checks their form, not where the number came from.

The magnitude gate (v2.15d) asks the model once, without retrieval, for a rough estimate; whether the evidence-based estimate is more than 2x above or below it can carry the model's memory of the target into one repair. The rough number itself never enters a computation or a prompt; the estimate before that repair is kept in judge_rounds[-1].magnitude_checks[0]. The gate is off in the own-history ablation.
